questions.stem: At a confined-space gas assessment, a supervisor proposes: "Bulk density of the unopened product container". The underlying case is: A process produces irregular mineral particles with the same mass but different shapes. The industrial hygienist must predict where they may deposit in the respiratory tract. Which particle characteristic is most useful for this purpose? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Visible color under normal workplace lighting
Bulk density of the unopened product container
Aerodynamic diameter, because it reflects settling behavior rather than geometric size alone
The molecular weight of the mineral as if it were a gas
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Aerodynamic diameter combines size, shape, and density effects relevant to airborne motion and respiratory deposition; bulk appearance or molecular weight alone does not predict particle behavior.

The proposed response 'Bulk density of the unopened product container' remains incomplete or misapplies the controlling particle aerodynamic behavior principle.

questions.stem: At a welding-fume evaluation, a supervisor proposes: "Increase general room air movement so the dust is less visible near the saw". The underlying case is: A dry cutting operation generates a broad particle-size distribution containing respirable crystalline silica. Which control strategy most directly reduces the hazardous respirable fraction at the source? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: Issue disposable dust masks without evaluating exposure or fit
Increase general room air movement so the dust is less visible near the saw
Schedule the cutting at night while using the same uncontrolled process
Use effective wet methods or local exhaust at the cutting point and verify performance with exposure monitoring
questions.correctAnswerExplanation: Source controls such as wet cutting and local exhaust suppress or capture respirable particles before worker exposure; visibility, scheduling, and unverified respirators are not equivalent controls.

questions.stem: At a solvent-vapor investigation, a supervisor proposes: "Vapor pressure matters only after a solvent reaches its boiling point". The underlying case is: Two solvents have similar toxicity, but solvent A has a substantially higher vapor pressure at the process temperature. All other conditions are equal. Which conclusion is most defensible? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?

Solvent A will remain in the liquid phase longer because higher vapor pressure reduces evaporation
Both solvents must produce identical airborne concentrations because their toxicity is similar
Vapor pressure matters only after a solvent reaches its boiling point

questions.stem: At a combustible-dust walkthrough, a supervisor proposes: "Sample only at the ceiling because all gases rise after release". Include low locations and breathing-zone measurements while recognizing that turbulence and temperature can alter stratification
Place one fixed monitor at waist height and assume it represents every location
Use gas density to replace a site-specific ventilation and dispersion assessment

Carbon monoxide generation from spontaneous nitrogen combustion
Oxygen deficiency caused by displacement of air
Radiation exposure caused by the compressed-gas cylinder

questions.stem: At a gas-cylinder release analysis, a supervisor proposes: "The vapor cannot present a health hazard until it enters the flammable range". The underlying case is: A solvent has a lower flammable limit of 1% by volume and an upper flammable limit of 8%. A vapor reading is 0.5% by volume. What is the best interpretation? Which alternative is the most defensible correction?
options: The reading is above the upper flammable limit and therefore oxygen-free
The vapor cannot present a health hazard until it enters the flammable range
The atmosphere is permanently nonflammable because the current reading is below 1%

Only particles visible as an airborne cloud can participate in combustion
